quality_effect: Prevent title-plan and OS-map linework from being promoted to exact parcel-boundary measurement evidence.

official_sources.title: Practice guide 40 supplement 1: basis of Land Registry plans

verified_facts: HMLR cannot provide scaled measurements from title plans or OS mapping because mapping has specified accuracy tolerances.
A 1:1250 OS map line width roughly represents 0.3m on the ground.
A 1:2500 OS map line width roughly represents 0.6m on the ground.
Enlarging a map does not improve the original survey accuracy.
Copying, reducing or enlarging a plan can distort accuracy.
Most registered titles use general boundaries.
There is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio between a general title-plan boundary and the legal boundary.
Physical-feature precision depends on the source survey accuracy.
OS map lines indicate mapped features subject to survey limitations.
Legal boundary interpretation may require deeds and ground evidence beyond the title plan.
General-boundary red line must not be treated as an exact legal line.
Boundary measurement promotion therefore requires determined-boundary or equivalent exact evidence.
